messages:
Priya: Heads-up — nightly perf dashboard flagged a p95 latency jump (~28%) on the merge window for kernel selection path, starting at 02:07 UTC. link: https://dash.redwood/test/nightly
Sam: saw that. rolling 2h window shows spike aligns with merge of PR #4523 (kernel-selector heuristic tweak)
Anna: any CI perf failures for that merge?
ci-bot: PR #4523 CI: perf/regressions: p95_latency +26% (compare: base=main@a1b2c3 -> head=pr/4523@d4e5f6)
Priya: thanks. attaching quick flame from profiler run on canary: small but consistent kernel decision bounce that adds ~6-10ms per request at 512 seq
Mike: can you paste the profiler output?
Priya: sure — simplifying paste:
```
kernel_selector::select() 
  40% decision_hotpath
  30% weight_compute
  20% kv_cache_lookup
  10% other
-- observed extra calls to weight_compute when batch_size==1 after merge
```
Sam: interesting — weight_compute increase implies we're recomputing kernel weights instead of reusing table from prober
Anna: that could increase KV pressure too if selector asks for prefetched keys repeatedly
Priya: nightly KV miss rate increased from 3.1% -> 9.8% around same time window (observed on hotset metric)
ops-bot: alert: kv_cache_miss_rate > 5% for 15m on region-us-west-2
Mike: action plan? bisect the merge? revert? can we do a targeted rollback for the heuristic change only?
Sam: I started a local git-bisect yesterday anchored to main@a1b2c3..pr/4523 to find offending commit; next step is to build minimized repro to run unit perf tests
Priya: I ran a quick bisect on canary — narrowed to commit d4e5f6a (heuristic refactor: prefer_weighted_kernel_when_entropy_low)
Anna: oks — is there a config toggle we can flip? maybe fall back to previous heuristic for latency-sensitive routes
Sam: yes, selector has runtime flag selector.prefer_weighted=false — we can flip at rollout to mitigate quickly
Mike: do we have a playbook to flip and redeploy?
Priya: toggle + restart of selector-service pod pool in canary works, but need to roll this to prod carefully (affects batching heuristics)
Anna: let's do canary toggle first and run load test (synthetic p95 check)
Sam: I'll open a quick rollback PR that sets selector.prefer_weighted=false behind trial flag and patch deployment manifests
Priya: also capturing perf compare output from CI: 
```
CI perf compare --base main@a1b2c3 --head pr/4523@d4e5f6 
Metric p95: 120.3ms -> 154.9ms (+28.9%)
KV miss rate: 3.1% -> 9.8%
Batching efficiency: tokens_per_gpu -3.6%
```
Mike: yikes. tokens_per_gpu drop explains cost regression too. Possibly kernel choice prevents coalescing across similar requests
Anna: note: batcher logs showed increased fragmentation (more singletons) at 02:06-02:10 UTC. attach snippet
Priya: snippet:
```
[02:06] batcher: created 156 batches, singletons=47 (prev-nightly avg=12)
[02:07] selector: selected kernel K2 for 60% of requests, was K1 previously
```
Sam: that selection skew is key. K2 has worse cold-KV behavior and higher per-decision cost
Mike: proposal: flip selector.prefer_weighted=false in canary now, run 30m smoke, then promote to prod if p95 drops back under 10% increase threshold
Anna: agreed. also file follow-up to revert heuristic refactor or rework to memoize weight_compute results across invocations
Priya: I'll run the canary toggle now and post smoke numbers in 20m
Sam: I'll keep bisect/branch in case we need full revert (PR #4530 prepared)
ci-bot: perf-smoke triggered for selector-toggle (canary) — run id smoke-2026-03-18-02:40
Priya: smoke results: p95 back to +4% vs baseline, KV miss down to 3.6%, tokens_per_gpu regained ~+1.2%
Mike: nice. please proceed with staged rollout and add a quick feature flag audit to ensure default is safe
Anna: put a postmortem ticket and include perf test that asserts no p95 delta >10% for selector changes
Priya: created issue INF-6189 with notes and links to CI traces and perf logs
Sam: thanks — will follow up with a small patch to memoize weight_compute and add unit perf test
Mike: appreciated. closing loop: revert not necessary now, but keep PR #4530 ready if something else pops up
Priya: tl;dr: post-merge heuristic tweak caused kernel selection skew -> weight recompute + KV miss spike -> p95 up. Canary toggle mitigated, staged rollout in progress. :thumbsup:
